\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{شہزادہ} (shahzādā)}{شہزادہ (shahzādā)}]{\ur{شہزادہ} (shahzādā) — a prince}

\label{lesson:UR-C328-shahzada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to bite (of a snake), then the Urdu for a diamond.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{شہزادہ}}
\textbf{\ur{شہزادہ}} — \emph{shahzādā} — \textquotedblleft{}a prince\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{شہزادہ} \ur{رات} \ur{کو} \ur{شہر} \ur{میں} \ur{گھومتا} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shahzādā rāt ko shahr meṅ ghūmtā thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The prince used to walk about the city at night.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{شہزادہ}} (\emph{shahzādā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{shāhzāda}, \textquotedblleft{}born of a king\textquotedblright{}, built from \emph{shāh}, a king, and \emph{zāda}, \textquotedblleft{}born\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shahzādā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shahzādā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shahzādā rāt ko shahr meṅ ghūmtā thā.} — The prince used to walk about the city at night.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to bite (of a snake), then the Urdu for a diamond, then say \emph{shahzādā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{شہزادہ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A prince\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بھیس} (bhes)}{بھیس (bhes)}]{\ur{بھیس} (bhes) — a disguise}

\label{lesson:UR-C328-bhes}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a diamond, then the Urdu for a prince.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بھیس}}
\textbf{\ur{بھیس}} — \emph{bhes} — \textquotedblleft{}a disguise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{کسان} \ur{کا} \ur{بھیس} \ur{بدلا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{us ne kisān kā bhes badlā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He disguised himself as a farmer.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بھیس}} (\emph{bhes}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{bhes}, \textquotedblleft{}dress, an assumed appearance\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{vēṣa} (CDIAL 12129). \textbf{\ur{بھیس} \ur{بدلنا}} is to put on a disguise.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{آزمانا} (āzmānā)}{آزمانا (āzmānā)}]{\ur{آزمانا} (āzmānā) — to put to the test}

\label{lesson:UR-C328-azmana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a prince, then the Urdu for a disguise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{آزمانا}}
\textbf{\ur{آزمانا}} — \emph{āzmānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to put to the test\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{شہزادے} \ur{نے} \ur{لوگوں} \ur{کو} \ur{آزمایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shahzāde ne logoṅ ko āzmāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The prince put the people to the test.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{دوست} \ur{کو} \ur{آزمایا}, \emph{us ne dost ko āzmāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{آزمانا}} (\emph{āzmānā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{āzmā-}, the stem of \emph{āzmūdan}, \textquotedblleft{}to test\textquotedblright{}, with the Urdu verb ending.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{فریب} (fareb)}{فریب (fareb)}]{\ur{فریب} (fareb) — deceit; a false show}

\label{lesson:UR-C328-fareb}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a disguise, then the Urdu for to put to the test.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{فریب}}
\textbf{\ur{فریب}} — \emph{fareb} — \textquotedblleft{}deceit; a false show\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{لوگ} \ur{اس} \ur{کے} \ur{فریب} \ur{میں} \ur{آ} \ur{گئے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{log us ke fareb meṅ ā gae.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
People fell for his deceit.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{فریب}} (\emph{fareb}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{farēb}, \textquotedblleft{}deceit\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\ur{فریب} \ur{میں} \ur{آنا}} is to be taken in.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بہکانا} (bahkānā)}{بہکانا (bahkānā)}]{\ur{بہکانا} (bahkānā) — to lead astray}

\label{lesson:UR-C328-bahkana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to put to the test, then the Urdu for deceit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بہکانا}}
\textbf{\ur{بہکانا}} — \emph{bahkānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to lead astray\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{وزیر} \ur{نے} \ur{بادشاہ} \ur{کو} \ur{بہکایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{vazīr ne bādshāh ko bahkāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The minister led the king astray.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{بچے} \ur{کو} \ur{بہکایا}, \emph{us ne bachche ko bahkāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بہکانا}} (\emph{bahkānā}) is the causing form of \emph{bahaknā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be misled\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists for Hindi under Sanskrit \emph{vyáthatē} (CDIAL 12164): to make someone lose the way.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to put to the test, then the Urdu for deceit, then say \emph{bahkānā} again
\end{itemize}
